paragraphs: Along a chain of coastal islands, colonies of a ground-nesting tern declined sharply during the 1990s on every island that American mink, escaped from fur farms, had reached by swimming from the mainland; colonies on islands the mink had not reached held steady. Wildlife managers concluded that predation by mink had caused the declines and began trapping the animals. Within a decade the mink had been eliminated from most of the affected islands, yet tern numbers there have recovered only partially. The managers attribute the sluggish recovery to the terns' habit of returning to breed where they were raised, a habit that delays the recolonization of abandoned sites.
